text: {"final": {"verdict": "accept", "reason": "The script matches the actual APIs: delivery_status() returns the gateway's {id: status} dict and the script selects only 'failed' ids; sent_messages() returns SmsMessage objects with .id/.household_id/.template_id/.params; queue_sms(household_id, template_id, params) re-renders the same text and looks up the registered phone, raising ValueError for sms_ok=False households, which the script catches and reports instead of aborting. Delivered (and missing-status) messages are never re-queued. The idempotency guard is sound: re-sent messages get new ids with no status entry, so signatures built from messages absent from the status file correctly detect prior re-sends, and the set is updated during the loop so a single run can't double-send. record('sms_batch', actor, ref=...) is a valid audit event with the required actor and ref, and is called once after sending. Nothing existing is broken — the script only appends via queue_sms and audit.record."}}
reasoning:
Check the idempotency logic. The script's resent_signatures: messages whose id is not in status (no status entry). But wait — the original failed messages DO have status entries ("failed"). Re-sent messages have new ids with no status entry. So the signature set is correct: messages with no status entry are re-sends (or new messages queued after the status file was written). Hmm — but could there be messages queued after the status snapshot that are NOT re-sends of failed messages? E.g., new messages queued during the current cycle would have no status entry and would be in resent_signatures. If a new message happens to have the same household/template/params as a failed original, it would be wrongly skipped. That's an edge case; but the ticket says run once. The idempotency guard could over-skip if a legitimate new message matches. But is that a bug that breaks the ticket? The ticket says run once; the guard is defensive. If a new message with same household/template/params was queued after the status snapshot, the failed original would be skipped — meaning a household doesn't get its re-send. But actually, would that household get a text? Yes — the new message with same content was already queued/sent. So the household still gets the text. Not a double-text issue. Actually the guard is reasonable.

But wait — there's a subtle issue: the guard also matches messages queued after the original that are NOT re-sends. Consider: original failed message SMS-00002 (DELIVERY_MOVED to household X). Later, a new DELIVERY_MOVED to household X with same params was queued (e.g., another cycle). Then the re-send is skipped. But the household did receive that later text with same content. Fine.

Another check: `record("sms_batch", ACTOR, ref=...)` — record requires ref; provided. Event "sms_batch" is valid.

Check `delivery_status` returns dict; failed_ids from items where value == "failed". Good.

Check `by_id` — sent_messages returns SmsMessage with .id. Good.

Check queue_sms signature: queue_sms(household_id, template_id, params, *, now=None). Called with three positional args. Good.

Check feature("sms_enabled") — if SMS disabled, RuntimeError not caught. Ticket doesn't mention; presumably enabled.

Check store paths — script uses relative imports; fine.

One concern: the idempotency check `m.id not in status` — messages with no status entry include re-sends AND any message queued after the gateway recorded status. The docstring in delivery_status says "New messages have no entry yet." So this is per the plan's own description. The plan step P1 described exactly this approach. The item matches the plan.

Also check: does the script handle the case where a re-sent message itself failed? Not required.

Check `tuple(sorted(m.params.items()))` — params values could be unhashable? They're strings from templates. Fine.

Check print of delivered count — cosmetic.

One more: `record` is only called if sent — plan says "after sending, record one sms_batch audit event". Fine.

Potential issue: the script imports `from audit.log import record` — audit/log.py exists. `from notifications.sms import ...` — exists.

Does the script need to check that re-sent messages themselves might appear in a future status? Not relevant.

Edge: what if the same failed message's original is also in resent_signatures because... original has id in status (failed), so not included. Good.

What about messages whose id is in status but status value is something else like "pending"? Only "failed" selected. Good.

I think accept. Maybe check store.read_jsonl / append_jsonl exist? Reasonably confident. Also check config settings feature function exists — used by sms.py itself, fine.

One thing: the script's idempotency could wrongly skip if a household legitimately received an identical message after the original failed — but then they got the text, so "done when" is still satisfied (they get a text with the same message... well, they got it earlier via the new message). Acceptable.

Verdict: accept.
